unsdg.blocker: DATA-INTEGRITY blocker (pre-existing, in our own published file — NOT an upstream/URL problem): the published parquet's dedup key (series_key, obs_date) is NOT unique. jobs\ingest_unsdg.py truncates each series' dimensions to the first 3 (dim_parts[:3]) and collapses every period to Dec-31, so observations differing only in a 4th+ dimension share one (series_key,obs_date) with different values — e.g. SE_ADT_ACTS:400|Age=ALLAGE|Location=URBAN|Sex=BOTHSEX has 36 distinct values on 2024-12-31. 352,671 of 3,175,479 rows (11.1%) are such collapsible duplicates; the file dedups to 2,822,808 distinct pairs (88.9%). Therefore ANY correct S1 merge with dedup_keys=(series_key,obs_date) collapses those rows and trips merge's never-shrink guard (88.9% < 97% min_ratio). merge_and_write leaves the existing file untouched on the refusal, so update returns partial (after==before), not data loss. The upstream SDG API is healthy (Series/List 200, Series/Data 200 with real records). REAL FIX is upstream and out of scope for this fetcher (changes shared files/data): make series_key carry ALL dimensions (drop the [:3] truncation) so (series_key,obs_date) is unique, then re-ingest all 713 series. Until then this source can only ever publish via merge as 'partial'.

vdem.blocker: vparty.parquet series_key scheme is incompatible with S1 (series_key,obs_date) dedup. vparty is a country-year-PARTY cube but its series_key "VDEM:{var}:{country}" omits the party dimension, so all parties in a country-year share one (series_key,obs_date). Deduping collapses 2,242,785 party-level rows -> 619,459, tripping merge's never-shrink @0.97. The original ingest_vdem.py wrote vparty with plain pq.write_table (NO dedup), which is why the existing parquet has the duplicates. To make vparty S1-refreshable the party id (v2paid/pf_party_id) must be embedded in series_key, e.g. "VDEM:{var}:{country}:{party_id}", and the existing parquet re-ingested under that scheme. vdem.parquet (the 77.4M-row core) is genuine country-year (0 collisions) and merges cleanly. The fetcher does NOT fake success or weaken the guard: it surfaces vparty as a structural sub-unit and returns partial while keeping both files untouched.
